lastCompletedStory.title: Persist notify fields to [notify], never the API key

nextStoryContext: mergeConfigChoices (src/commands/config.ts) now persists choices.resendRecipient/resendFrom into a [notify] TomlSection additively via mergeIntoConfig, mirroring the [plan]/[ship] blocks. Empty-string or undefined resendRecipient/resendFrom are treated as 'leave unset' per the wizard contract documented in ConfigScreen.tsx (US-003): the helper skips the mergeIntoConfig call entirely when neither field is non-empty, so no empty [notify] table is ever written. resend_api_key is NEVER emitted by this write path (confirmed: the only production writer of resend_api_key into project.toml remains a human hand-edit; src/config/models.ts's readResendConfig only READS it for backward-compat, alongside the canonical RESEND_API_KEY env var). Refactor note: mergeConfigChoices's cognitive complexity hit biome's ceiling (15) once the [notify] branch was added (20 with inline logic, 16 after extracting buildNotifyUpdate as a pure helper); the fix that got it under the ceiling was extracting TWO MORE pieces into standalone functions -- persistMergeMode(configPath, choices, mergeModeOpts) (the [ship]+applyMergeMode block) and rewriteFrontmatterModels(cwd, choices) (the frontmatter-rewrite loop) -- leaving mergeConfigChoices itself as a thin sequence of calls. If a future story adds another conditional [section] write here, extract it as its own named function from the start rather than inlining, since the ceiling is already tight at 4 near-independent conditional blocks. This story's write-path tests live in test/commands/config-persist.test.ts (extended, not a new file): asserts [notify] keys land correctly, empty/undefined choices write nothing, pre-existing [notify] keys (e.g. resend_recipient from a prior run) are preserved/updated additively, and the raw serialized TOML string never contains the substring 'resend_api_key'.

officialDocsValidated.lib: none (TOML spec, no external npm lib touched)
officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed TOML spec: an empty table header with no keys is valid, parseable TOML ('[empty_table]' alone). Not load-bearing for this story since mergeConfigChoices deliberately skips the mergeIntoConfig call when [notify] would be empty (per the wizard's 'leave unset' contract), but confirms the alternative (writing an empty [notify] block) would also have been spec-valid if a future story needs it.
